o1.biggest_strength: It turns the data into the right hiring system: APAC/00:00-08:00 UTC coverage, a plain weekend warning, no experience requirements, and a short written customer reply as the main screen.
o1.biggest_mistake: The salary is included but not as high up as it should be for this brand and brief.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the $82,000 salary into the first screen of the post and trim a little so the published version is tighter.

o2.biggest_strength: It leads with the salary, states the overnight need and weekend rotation plainly, and correctly drops degrees, tool experience and years in support.
o2.biggest_mistake: The application writing prompt gives no internal facts to solve, so it tests tone more than the strongest signal: fixing the customer's actual problem in writing.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a concrete application exercise with enough facts to diagnose and solve the issue, plus the exact longer exercise and call questions so the team can run it tomorrow.

reason: Both are strong and on-brand, but Output 1 is more operationally ready: it includes a real application exercise, a second-stage exercise, call questions, reviewer calibration, and a scorecard tied tightly to the predictive signals. Output 2 is cleaner in places, especially salary placement, but needs more work before the team can use it.
